I used the function B.kappa = inla.mesh.basis(mesh, type = "sph.harm"), it returns me an error: Only know how to make spherical harmonics on S2. messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Creating a mesh on a sphere S2
parts:
Hi!
The code currently only supports calculating spherical harmonics on a proper spherical mesh. For global models, the intended usage is to build meshes that live on the curved space, so that distances and connectivity are correct. Long-lat coordinates are usually very inappropriate, unless the study region is very local, and close to the equator. To build a such a mesh, simply convert Lon-lat to Cartesian xyz and supply that to inla.mesh.create.

That being said, the following workaround can be used if you really need o calculate spherical harmonics in Lon-lat in R2:
1. Create your flat mesh.
2. Create another mesh,call it mesh2, on the sphere, as described above, using the mesh points mesh$loc from step 1., and refine=false.
3. Calculate sph.harm on mesh2, and index by mesh2$idx$loc to get the values for the flat mesh.

More documentation for all this is on its way.

Finn L
